  | 9 to 16 | 64.4 | 87.4 | 62.8 | 109.7 |

  What changing `inner` does to a two-thread bench is a systematic effect and not noise about a
  line, so the regression can give neither the sample's overhead nor the step's cost for them.
- `slp-futex-slptfe` sleeps at every look, and its passes differ by up to 10% at one `inner`, so
  this sweep says nothing of its shape.

## Drawn per sample

A run at a fixed `inner` repeats one burst length, so the sweep cannot say whether a two-thread
bench's cost follows the length or the repetition. `--inner 1-16` draws each sample's length
from the span, and the record holds the samples and their summed time at each length.

- Source: commit `124244db`, jj change `vrxrlwwy`, a clean tree, `feat: inner drawn per sample
  from a range`, `iiac-perf-dev` 0.28.24-2, binary `f53a7f480a66675f`, built on the 3900X.
- The same host, placements, and benches as the sweep. Two passes of five runs, tagged `pass`,
  2026-10-08T17:30Z to 17:34Z, `--run-sleep 100-200ms`:
  - the three two-thread benches on `ccx` at `--inner 1-16` and at `--inner 1-32`
  - `min-now` on `smt` at `--inner 20-120`
  - the two spinning benches at `--inner 7` and at `--inner 8`, fixed, as a control on the
    binary
- Records, every switch count zero:
  [records/inner-drawn-7600x.jsonl](../records/inner-drawn-7600x.jsonl), 110 runs.

The control reads as the landed binary did: `sos-futex-spntfe` 76.0 ns at 7 and 67.0 ns at 8,
`so-spntfe` 71.1 and 70.6 ns. So the new binary's fixed loop measures what the old one did.

## What linear-regression says

`iiac-perf-dev linear-regression records/inner-sweep-7600x.jsonl` and the same on
`records/inner-drawn-7600x.jsonl`. The command is a simple linear regression of sample time on
`inner`, by ordinary least squares. It refits each half of the lengths and names a cost only
where the two slopes agree within 1%, "a line holds". The slope is in ns a step and the
intercept in ns:

| bench | `inner` | slope | intercept | halves apart % | period | a line |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `min-now` | fixed, 20 to 120 | 18.264 | 18.53 | 0.01 | | holds |
| `min-now` | drawn, 20-120 | 18.256 | 18.16 | 0.02 | none | holds |
| `so-spntfe` | fixed, 1 to 16 | 70.435 | 5.78 | 5.53 | none | does not hold |
| `so-spntfe` | drawn, 1-16 | 74.438 | 7.08 | 5.00 | none | does not hold |
| `so-spntfe` | drawn, 1-32 | 68.165 | 25.58 | 0.95 | none | holds |
| `sos-futex-spntfe` | fixed, 1 to 16 | 69.557 | 18.18 | 6.25 | 4 | does not hold |
| `sos-futex-spntfe` | drawn, 1-16 | 76.155 | 11.96 | 2.69 | none | does not hold |
| `sos-futex-spntfe` | drawn, 1-32 | 69.968 | 28.87 | 1.36 | none | does not hold |

`slp-futex-slptfe` is left out: in all three its runs scatter too much for the halves to say.

- One thread: both ways give `min-now` 18.26 ns a step and about 18.4 ns a sample, the two
  slopes 0.008 ns apart. The regression holds and the two ways agree.
- The period of 4 followed the repetition. Fixed, `sos-futex-spntfe`'s residuals by `inner`
  modulo 4 are -31.7, +14.9, +0.3 and +16.4 ns a sample, a period that accounts for 71% of the
  other pass's residual scatter. Drawn over 1-16 they are -0.9, +1.4, -0.1 and -0.4 ns, and
  `linear-regression` finds no period in any drawn group.
- What is left is smooth. A sample of one step sits 10 ns over the line for `sos-futex-spntfe`
  and 15 ns for `so-spntfe`, the next few under it, and from about 8 steps the level is flat
  to 0.3 ns. So the short lengths bend the line, and over 1-32, where they are a smaller share,
  the halves come within 1.4%.
- The slope depends on the span, and on the run. Over 1-16 every run of ten reads within 0.4 ns
  of 74.4 ns a step for `so-spntfe` and of 76.2 ns for `sos-futex-spntfe`. Over 1-32 eight runs
  of ten read 68.1 to 68.6 and 69.8 to 70.2 ns, and two read 72.3 and 74.1, and 74.6 and 74.8
  ns. So a two-thread bench runs at one of two rates about 6 ns a step apart, a whole run at
  one of them, and the span moves the odds. We think it is a state the two threads settle
  into, and nothing here says what sets it.
- At either rate the ring that can sleep reads slower than the spin-only one by about the same
  amount, 1.7 ns a step over 1-16 and 1.8 ns over 1-32, 2.3% and 2.6%. `linear-regression`
  names no cost for three of those four groups, so this is a pointer and not a measurement.

So for one thread the regression gives the step's cost and the sample's overhead. For two
threads drawing the lengths removes the period, and what remains, a bend at short lengths and
two rates a run may land on, still keeps a line from holding in most groups.

## With the overhead taken off

The harness wraps a sample in the same clock reads whatever it times, so its overhead is one
number for a host. `linear-regression` takes it from `min-now`'s intercept, 18.53 ns from the
fixed counts and 18.16 ns from the drawn lengths, and takes it off each length's sample. What
is left over `inner` is the cost of a step at that length, the `step ns` column:

| bench | `inner` | step at 1 | lowest step, at | step at the longest |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `so-spntfe` | fixed, 1 to 16 | 71.92 | 62.79, 3 | 68.14 |
| `so-spntfe` | drawn, 1-32 | 78.55 | 68.29, 31 | 68.36 |
| `sos-futex-spntfe` | fixed, 1 to 16 | 74.02 | 64.19, 8 | 66.64 |
| `sos-futex-spntfe` | drawn, 1-32 | 80.18 | 70.20, 30 | 70.21 |

- Most of what a sample of one step read over a long one was the harness. The levels at `inner`
  1 were 90.5 and 92.6 ns, 21 and 25 ns over the levels at 16, and with the overhead off the
  step at 1 is 3.8 and 7.4 ns over the step at 16.
- Drawn, a sample of one step costs about 10 ns more than a step of a long burst, for both
  rings. Over 1-32 `so-spntfe` holds a line, and its intercept less the overhead is 7.42 ns,
  what the ring pays once a sample. We think it is the ring starting a burst.
- The controls at `--inner 7` and `8` are two lengths, too few to regress, and are given a step
  by the subtraction: `so-spntfe` 68.44 and 68.14 ns, `sos-futex-spntfe` 73.36 and 64.65 ns, the
  period of 4 still in the second.
- Whether a clock read costs the same after a ring step as after another clock read is not
  measured, so the overhead is `min-now`'s and is taken as the ring's.

## What it does not hold

- `Multi`, the `smt` pair for two threads, and `inner` past 16. A larger sweep was stopped for
  its length, and its one pass, 800 runs, is not committed.
- The 3900X and the Pi 5.
- Why repeating one burst length gives the ring that can sleep a period of 4, and what sets
  which of the two rates a run lands on.

44:## The names
45-
46-```
47-zcr-mpsc-v4-<threads>-<mode>-<wait choice>[-spnt<spin time>][-slpt<sleep time>]
48-```
49-
50-A name states everything that changes what the bench measures. What the ring is comes first and
51-is always said, used or not, since a ring pays for what it is built as. What a receiver does
52-comes after, and a time of zero is left out, not doing a thing costing nothing.
53-
54-- The ring:
55-  - `<mode>` is `single`, or `multi-<n>seg` over `n` segments.
56-  - `<wait choice>` is the choice and then its waiter: `so` for `SpinOnly`, `slp-futex` for
57-    `Sleep<Futex>`, and `sos-futex` for `SpinOrSleep<Futex>`. v3's ring has a wake where v4's
58-    has a choice, and its name has nothing there for `NoWake` and `futex` for `Futex`.
59-- A receiver, by zc-ring-x1's words `spin_time` and `sleep_time`:
60-  - `spnt` is how long it spins at an empty ring, `spntfe` forever. A name without one does not
61-    spin and sleeps at once.
62-  - `slpt` is how long it then sleeps, `slptfe` until woken. A name without one does not sleep.
63-  - The two are one receive call's. A receive that gives up empty is made again, a round trip
64-    needing its message, so `spnt1us` with no sleep after it is a spin without end that reads
65-    the clock at each look and returns every microsecond.
66-- So `zcr-mpsc-v4-2t-single-sos-futex-spntfe` is two threads, a `Single` ring able to spin or
67-  sleep on a futex, and receivers that spin forever and so never use it.
68-- The twelve twins are v3's shapes, `1t` and `2t` by `multi-2seg`, `multi-1seg`, and `single`, each
69-  `-so-spntfe` over `SpinOnly` and `-sos-futex-spntfe` over `SpinOrSleep<Futex>`. They wait by
70-  `send_spin` and `recv_spin` with `Ticks::FOREVER`, where v3's benches pass `policy::spin` to
71-  `send` and `reserve_slot_with`.

input.new_string:
`linear-regression` says of both.

## Terms

What is measured:

- **Step**: the operation a bench times. For a ring one message sent and received, for `min-now`
  one clock read.
- **Sample**: one timed stretch, a clock read before and after `inner` steps back to back. Its
  time, the sample time, is in ns.
- **`inner`**: the steps in one sample, also called its length. `--inner 7` fixes it for a run,
  `--inner 1-16` draws each sample's from the span, and with neither the harness sizes it.
  "Fixed" and "drawn" in the tables say which.
- **Run**: one process measuring one bench, thousands of samples, its result the mean.
- **Pass**: one time through the list of `inner` values, `a` or `b`, the second the first
  reversed.
- **Level**: a sample's time divided by `inner`, in ns, what iiac-perf reports for a bench. It is
  a step's cost with the harness overhead shared out over the steps.
- **Harness overhead**: what a sample costs beyond its steps, the clock reads around them, about
  18 ns on the 7600X. It is the same whatever the bench, so it is measured once, by `min-now`.

What `linear-regression` reports, a line fitted through sample time against `inner`:

- **Slope**: what one more step adds to a sample, ns a step, the cost of a step where a line
  holds.
- **Intercept**: what a sample of no steps would take, ns. For `min-now` it is the harness
  overhead, and for a ring the overhead plus what the ring pays once a sample.
- **Residual**: how far a length's sample time sits from the line, ns.
- **Halves apart**: the line refitted over the lower and the upper half of the lengths, and the
  two slopes' difference as a percent of the whole line's slope.
- **A line holds**: the halves are within 1% of each other, so every step costs about the same
  whatever the length and the slope and intercept mean what they say. Otherwise no cost is
  named.
- **Period**: residuals that repeat with `inner` modulo some k, found in one pass and scored by
  how much of the other pass's scatter they account for. "None" is looked for and not found,
  and blank is not looked for, as where the lengths are not consecutive.

The benches, whose names are decoded in full in [The
names](mpsc-v4-mode-waits.md#the-names):

- `min-now`: a single clock read and no ring, one thread.
- The two-thread benches are `zcr-mpsc-v4-2t-single-` and a tail, written here by the tail.
  `2t` is a sender and a receiver on two threads, and `single` a `Single` ring.
  - `so-spntfe`: a ring that can only spin, `SpinOnly`, its receiver spinning forever at an
    empty ring. "The spin-only one" in the text.
  - `sos-futex-spntfe`: a ring that can spin or sleep on a futex, `SpinOrSleep<Futex>`, its
    receiver spinning forever and so never sleeping. "The ring that can sleep" in the text.
  - `slp-futex-slptfe`: a ring that sleeps on a futex, `Sleep<Futex>`, its receiver sleeping
    until woken at every empty look.
  - `so` and `sos-futex` are those first two where a column has no room.
- Placements: `ccx` and `smt`, the CPUs given in [The sweep](#the-sweep).

## Terms

What is measured:

- **Step**: the operation a bench times. For a ring one message sent and received, for `min-now`
  one clock read.
- **Sample**: one timed stretch, a clock read before and after `inner` steps back to back. Its
  time, the sample time, is in ns.
- **`inner`**: the steps in one sample, also called its length. `--inner 7` fixes it for a run,
  `--inner 1-16` draws each sample's from the span, and with neither the harness sizes it.
  "Fixed" and "drawn" in the tables say which.
- **Run**: one process measuring one bench, thousands of samples, its result the mean.
- **Pass**: one time through the list of `inner` values, `a` or `b`, the second the first
  reversed.
- **Level**: a sample's time divided by `inner`, in ns, what iiac-perf reports for a bench. It is
  a step's cost with the harness overhead shared out over the steps.
- **Harness overhead**: what a sample costs beyond its steps, the clock reads around them, about
  18 ns on the 7600X. It is the same whatever the bench, so it is measured once, by `min-now`.

What `linear-regression` reports, a line fitted through sample time against `inner`:

- **Slope**: what one more step adds to a sample, ns a step, the cost of a step where a line
  holds.
- **Intercept**: what a sample of no steps would take, ns. For `min-now` it is the harness
  overhead, and for a ring the overhead plus what the ring pays once a sample.
- **Residual**: how far a length's sample time sits from the line, ns.
- **Halves apart**: the line refitted over the lower and the upper half of the lengths, and the
  two slopes' difference as a percent of the whole line's slope.
- **A line holds**: the halves are within 1% of each other, so every step costs about the same
  whatever the length and the slope and intercept mean what they say. Otherwise no cost is
  named.
- **Period**: residuals that repeat with `inner` modulo some k, found in one pass and scored by
  how much of the other pass's scatter they account for. "None" is looked for and not found,
  and blank is not looked for, as where the lengths are not consecutive.

The benches, whose names are decoded in full in [The
names](mpsc-v4-mode-waits.md#the-names):

- `min-now`: a single clock read and no ring, one thread.
- The two-thread benches are `zcr-mpsc-v4-2t-single-` and a tail, written here by the tail.
  `2t` is a sender and a receiver on two threads, and `single` a `Single` ring.
  - `so-spntfe`: a ring that can only spin, `SpinOnly`, its receiver spinning forever at an
    empty ring. "The spin-only one" in the text.
  - `sos-futex-spntfe`: a ring that can spin or sleep on a futex, `SpinOrSleep<Futex>`, its
    receiver spinning forever and so never sleeping. "The ring that can sleep" in the text.
  - `slp-futex-slptfe`: a ring that sleeps on a futex, `Sleep<Futex>`, its receiver sleeping
    until woken at every empty look.
  - `so` and `sos-futex` are those first two where a column has no room.

lastPrompt: The term level is sample-time/inner, would a benchmark expert or statistician use that term? In my mind it doesn't fit, I'd call it inner-loop-time.

content.text:
You're right that it doesn't fit. Neither a benchmark expert nor a statistician would use "level" for this number.

- **Benchmark tools** call sample time divided by `inner` the time per iteration or per operation. Go reports `ns/op`, JMH reports `ns/op` under `avgt`, and Criterion says "time per iteration".
- **For a statistician**, "level" is time-series vocabulary: the value a series fluctuates around, as in "a level shift". The project's drift and step detectors probably carried the word over. Used for one bench's per-step mean, it's in-house jargon.

I'm wary of "inner-loop-time", though. It can be read as the time of the whole inner loop, which is the sample time, the very thing it's divided out of. There's also a second number to name. With the overhead taken off, the note already has `step ns`, which is (sample − overhead) / `inner`. Both numbers are "per step", so the names need to tell them apart:

| quantity | now | suggestion |
|---|---|---|
| sample / `inner`, overhead shared in | level | time per step (`ns/step`) |
| (sample − overhead) / `inner` | step ns | net step time (`net ns/step`) |

Either way, it's more than a wording fix in this note. "level" is all through `notes/` and `README.md`, and it's a column header in `linear-regression`'s own output (`src/linear_regression.rs`, "level ns"). There are two ways to go:

1. **This rung defines the term, and the rename becomes a Todo entry.** The note's Terms section says plainly that "level" is this project's word for time per step, the overhead shared in, and that standard tools call it `ns/op`. A Todo entry then renames it across the code output and the notes as its own cycle. That matches the rule that convention work is its own cycle.
2. **Rename only in this note now.** The note would stop agreeing with the command's output and with the other notes until the wider rename happens.

I recommend option 1. Which do you want, and which name: "time per step", your "inner-loop-time", or something else?

message.content: option 1, time per step

A note defines its words in passing or not at all, and the definitions that exist are apart:

file.content:
# An inner sweep on the 7600X

A bench's level is a sample's time divided by `inner`, the steps timed back to back in the
sample, and the harness sizes `inner` by itself in every run. This file holds a sweep that fixes
`inner` by hand over a range, to show what the level does as it changes, from `feat: fit, the
cost of a step from samples of many lengths` (2026-10-08). The records are what the
`linear-regression` subcommand, `lr` for short and first named `fit`, is written against. Below
the sweep are runs that draw `inner` per sample, taken once the harness could, and what
`linear-regression` says of both.

## Terms

What is measured:

- **Step**: the operation a bench times. For a ring one message sent and received, for `min-now`
  one clock read.
- **Sample**: one timed stretch, a clock read before and after `inner` steps back to back. Its
  time, the sample time, is in ns.
- **`inner`**: the steps in one sample, also called its length. `--inner 7` fixes it for a run,
  `--inner 1-16` draws each sample's from the span, and with neither the harness sizes it.
  "Fixed" and "drawn" in the tables say which.
- **Run**: one process measuring one bench over many samples, its result their mean.
- **Pass**: one time through the list of `inner` values, `a` or `b`, the second the first
  reversed.
- **Level**: a sample's time divided by `inner`, in ns, what iiac-perf reports for a bench. It is
  a step's cost with the harness overhead shared out over the steps. The standard term is time
  per step, `ns/op` in Go's and JMH's benchmarks, and "level" is this project's word for it
  until a rename reaches the code and every note.
- **Harness overhead**: what a sample costs beyond its steps, the clock reads around them, about
  18 ns on the 7600X. It is the same whatever the bench, so it is measured once, by `min-now`.

What `linear-regression` reports, a line fitted through sample time against `inner`:

content.text:
"Variable" leaves out what makes the drawn runs work. Each sample's length is picked uniformly at random from the span (`src/inner.rs:70`, `src/harness.rs:663`), and the randomness is what removed the period of 4. A run whose length varied in a fixed cycle, say 1, 2, …, 16 again and again, would also be "variable", but it repeats a pattern, and a pattern like that is what we think caused the period. So the word should say random, not just "changes".

If "drawn" doesn't read well, I'd suggest **fixed and random**. It's plain, and a statistician reads "random length" as "picked by chance". The one catch is that "fixed and random" is also a stats term, fixed versus random effects, but the context makes it unlikely anyone confuses the two. "Randomized" is another option.

The word also appears in about 14 places outside this note: `src/harness.rs`, `src/inner.rs`, the `linear-regression` output and other notes. So it would be the same split as "level": change this note now, and add the code and the other notes to the rename Todo entry, renamed to cover both words.

Which do you want: keep "drawn", switch to "random", or switch to "variable" anyway?

A bench's time per step is a sample's time divided by `inner`, the steps timed back to back in
the sample, and the harness sizes `inner` by itself in every run. This file holds a sweep that
fixes `inner` by hand over a range, to show what the time per step does as it changes, from `feat: fit, the
cost of a step from samples of many lengths` (2026-10-08). The records are what the
---
with each other and with the session in [mpsc-v4-mode-waits.md](mpsc-v4-mode-waits.md) on
two-thread benches at cross-core placements, by more than their claims allowed. Three probes on
the 7600X `ccx` pair, on `zcr-mpsc-v4-2t-single-sos-futex-spntfe`, found what moved the time per step.
Their records are not committed:
---
The time per step falls as `inner` grows and never settles. A line through sample time against `inner`,
fitted by hand, has a slope of 18.264 ns a step in each pass and an intercept of 18.61 ns in pass
a and 18.57 ns in pass b. So a sample costs about one clock read beyond its steps, and the time
per step carries that cost divided by `inner`.

benchmark tool nor a statistician uses it so: Go and JMH say `ns/op`, Criterion time per

  per step, so it takes a name that says the overhead is off, "net time per step" the first
  thought.

content.content:
### What one step costs

A bench's level is a sample's time divided by `inner`, the steps
timed back to back in the sample, so it carries a share of what the
sample itself costs, about one clock read. `linear-regression`,
`lr` for short, separates the two. It needs samples of several
lengths, so collect with `--inner` as a span, each sample drawing
its length from it, and record the runs:

```

On renaming the file:

- **Keep the `.jsonl` extension, not `.json`.** The file is JSON Lines, one record per line, as are all the other files in `records/`.
- **Put "inner" first: `inner-random-7600x.jsonl`.** It then sits next to its fixed counterpart, `inner-sweep-7600x.jsonl`, in a listing, and the pair reads as two kinds of `inner` run. `random-inner-7600x.jsonl` works but sorts away from it.
- **The rename is cheap.** Only `TODO.md` and `notes/inner-sweep.md` refer to the file, and jj records it as a rename, so its history follows.
- **One thing stays behind.** Each of the 110 records carries the path it was first written to, `~/iiac-perf-data/inner-drawn-20261008/inner-drawn-7600x.jsonl`, in its run configuration. That's a record of where it came from, and records aren't edited, so it keeps the old name. It's harmless, just a mismatch someone might notice.
- **Where it goes:** it could fit in this rung, since both files that refer to it are already being edited here and the note would then be consistent. Or it could go with the code under the rename Todo entry, which keeps this rung strictly docs. I lean towards this rung.

In short: "inner random per sample" for the output line, `inner-random-7600x.jsonl` for the file name, and old records keep the path they were written to.

content.text:
No, a sweep isn't a run. In this note a sweep is the whole experiment, made of many runs:

- **A run** is one process measuring one bench at one setting, `--inner 7` for example.
- **The sweep** is the set of runs that steps the fixed `inner` across a range, one run per value. It's 1 to 16 for the two-thread benches and 20 to 120 for `min-now`, over two passes, 336 runs in all. Within a run `inner` never changes; across the sweep it covers the range.

The note holds one sweep, plus a second set of 110 runs that is not a sweep. In those runs each sample picks its `inner` at random, so no value is held fixed and nothing is stepped.

So the opening is misleading in two ways. "A sweep that fixes `inner` by hand over a range" makes it sound like one fixed value. And "Below the sweep are runs that…" reads as if the second set is also a sweep. I'd rewrite it and add the term:

> A bench's time per step is a sample's time divided by `inner`, the steps timed back to back in the sample, and the harness sizes `inner` by itself in every run. This file holds two sets of runs on the 7600X, from `feat: fit, the cost of a step from samples of many lengths` (2026-10-08), to show what the time per step does as `inner` changes. The first is a sweep, each run at one fixed `inner` and the runs stepping it across a range. The second, taken once the harness could, has each sample pick its `inner` at random from a span. The `linear-regression` subcommand, `lr` for short and first named `fit`, is written against both, and the file ends with what it says of them.

And in Terms, after Pass:

> - **Sweep**: a set of runs that steps a fixed `inner` across a range, each run at one value. The sweep here is 336 runs, two passes of three runs a bench at each value.

Shall I make those two edits?

content.text:
I'd frame the finding a little differently, because "reduced the standard deviation" isn't quite what the data shows, and a statistician reading the title would expect it to mean exactly that.

**What we found:**
- **The problem wasn't scatter.** Runs at one fixed `inner` were already tight: 27 or more of each 30 within 0.6 ns. The problem was a systematic effect. The time per step depends on which `inner` the harness happens to pick. `sos-futex-spntfe` read 71.1 ns at 6 and 75.7 ns at 7, so two invocations sized differently disagreed by far more than their claims allowed. A statistician would call that bias, not variance.
- **Randomizing removed the pattern.** The period of 4 was gone. Over 1-16, every run read within 0.4 ns of the same value, so the result no longer depends on one lucky or unlucky value.
- **It didn't make everything tighter.** Over 1-32, a run lands on one of two rates about 6 ns apart. That's a new run-to-run spread, larger than anything at fixed `inner`.
- **Not yet shown:** that random `inner` makes separate invocations agree. Nothing here repeats invocations side by side. That test is the Todo entry "A span of inner from the auto value".

**So I'd put the finding in the title, but as "removes the dependence on `inner`" rather than "reduces stdev":**

> # Random inner removes the period of 4

**And an intro that runs problem, then finding, then limits:**

> Two invocations of one bench could disagree by more than their claims allowed, because the harness sizes `inner` itself and a two-thread bench's time per step depends on the value it picks: on the 7600X `ccx` pair `zcr-mpsc-v4-2t-single-sos-futex-spntfe` reads 71.1 ns a step at an `inner` of 6 and 75.7 ns at 7. This file holds what was taken to understand that, from `feat: fit, the cost of a step from samples of many lengths` (2026-10-08). A sweep, each run at one fixed `inner` and the runs stepping it across a range, shows the dependence has a period of 4. Runs in which each sample picks its `inner` at random from a span remove the period, so the result no longer hangs on one value. They do not make every run agree: over 1-32 a run lands on one of two rates about 6 ns a step apart. `linear-regression`, `lr` for short and first named `fit`, reads both, and with the harness overhead of about 18 ns taken off gives a step's cost where a line holds.

The "Why it was taken" section would then shrink, since the intro carries its story. The sweep term would go into Terms as proposed. I'd leave the file name `inner-sweep.md` alone, since other places link to it, unless you want that changed too.

In short: random `inner` stopped the result depending on which `inner` was picked, but didn't make runs less scattered. The title should claim the first and not the second.

Shall I make these edits?

content.content:
1	# An inner sweep on the 7600X
2	
3	A bench's time per step is a sample's time divided by `inner`, the steps timed back to back in
4	the sample, and the harness sizes `inner` by itself in every run. This file holds a sweep that
5	fixes `inner` by hand over a range, to show what the time per step does as it changes, from
6	`feat: fit, the cost of a step from samples of many lengths` (2026-10-08). The records are what
7	the `linear-regression` subcommand, `lr` for short and first named `fit`, is written against.
8	Below the sweep are runs that pick each sample's `inner` at random, taken once the harness could,
9	and what `linear-regression` says of both.
10	
11	## Terms
12	
13	What is measured:
14	
15	- **Step**: the operation a bench times. For a ring one message sent and received, for `min-now`
16	  one clock read.
17	- **Sample**: one timed stretch, a clock read before and after `inner` steps back to back. Its
18	  time, the sample time, is in ns.
19	- **`inner`**: the steps in one sample, also called its length. `--inner 7` fixes it for a run,
20	  `--inner 1-16` picks each sample's at random from the span, uniformly, and with neither the
21	  harness sizes it. "Fixed" and "random" in the tables say which.
22	- **Run**: one process measuring one bench over many samples, its result their mean.
23	- **Pass**: one time through the list of `inner` values, `a` or `b`, the second the first
24	  reversed.
25	- **Time per step**: a sample's time divided by `inner`, in ns, what iiac-perf reports for a
26	  bench. It is a step's cost with the harness overhead shared out over the steps, `ns/op` in Go's
27	  and JMH's benchmarks. The reports and the other notes call it the level until a rename reaches
28	  them.
29	- **Harness overhead**: what a sample costs beyond its steps, the clock reads around them, about
30	  18 ns on the 7600X. It is the same whatever the bench, so it is measured once, by `min-now`.
31	
32	What `linear-regression` reports, a line fitted through sample time against `inner`:
33	
34	- **Slope**: what one more step adds to a sample, ns a step, the cost of a step where a line
35	  holds.
36	- **Intercept**: what a sample of no steps would take, ns. For `min-now` it is the harness
37	  overhead, and for a ring the overhead plus what the ring pays once a sample.
38	- **Residual**: how far a length's sample time sits from the line, ns.
39	- **Halves apart**: the line refitted over the lower and the upper half of the lengths, and the
40	  two slopes' difference as a percent of the whole line's slope.
41	- **A line holds**: the halves are within 1% of each other, so every step costs about the same
42	  whatever the length and the slope and intercept mean what they say. Otherwise no cost is
43	  named.
44	- **Period**: residuals that repeat with `inner` modulo some k, found in one pass and scored by
45	  how much of the other pass's scatter they account for. "None" is looked for and not found,
46	  and blank is not looked for, as where the lengths are not consecutive.
47	
48	The benches, whose names are decoded in full in [The
49	names](mpsc-v4-mode-waits.md#the-names):
50	
51	- `min-now`: a single clock read and no ring, one thread.
52	- The two-thread benches are `zcr-mpsc-v4-2t-single-` and a tail, written here by the tail.
53	  `2t` is a sender and a receiver on two threads, and `single` a `Single` ring.

# An inner sweep on the 7600X

A bench's time per step is a sample's time divided by `inner`, the steps timed back to back in
the sample, and the harness sizes `inner` by itself in every run. This file holds a sweep that
fixes `inner` by hand over a range, to show what the time per step does as it changes, from
`feat: fit, the cost of a step from samples of many lengths` (2026-10-08). The records are what
the `linear-regression` subcommand, `lr` for short and first named `fit`, is written against.
Below the sweep are runs that pick each sample's `inner` at random, taken once the harness could,
and what `linear-regression` says of both.

## Terms

What is measured:

- **Step**: the operation a bench times. For a ring one message sent and received, for `min-now`
  one clock read.
- **Sample**: one timed stretch, a clock read before and after `inner` steps back to back. Its
  time, the sample time, is in ns.
- **`inner`**: the steps in one sample, also called its length. `--inner 7` fixes it for a run,
  `--inner 1-16` picks each sample's at random from the span, uniformly, and with neither the
  harness sizes it. "Fixed" and "random" in the tables say which.
- **Run**: one process measuring one bench over many samples, its result their mean.
- **Pass**: one time through the list of `inner` values, `a` or `b`, the second the first
  reversed.
- **Time per step**: a sample's time divided by `inner`, in ns, what iiac-perf reports for a
  bench. It is a step's cost with the harness overhead shared out over the steps, `ns/op` in Go's
  and JMH's benchmarks. The reports and the other notes call it the level until a rename reaches
  them.
- **Harness overhead**: what a sample costs beyond its steps, the clock reads around them, about
  18 ns on the 7600X. It is the same whatever the bench, so it is measured once, by `min-now`.

What `linear-regression` reports, a line fitted through sample time against `inner`:

- **Slope**: what one more step adds to a sample, ns a step, the cost of a step where a line
  holds.
- **Intercept**: what a sample of no steps would take, ns. For `min-now` it is the harness
  overhead, and for a ring the overhead plus what the ring pays once a sample.
- **Residual**: how far a length's sample time sits from the line, ns.
- **Halves apart**: the line refitted over the lower and the upper half of the lengths, and the
  two slopes' difference as a percent of the whole line's slope.
- **A line holds**: the halves are within 1% of each other, so every step costs about the same
  whatever the length and the slope and intercept mean what they say. Otherwise no cost is
  named.
- **Period**: residuals that repeat with `inner` modulo some k, found in one pass and scored by
  how much of the other pass's scatter they account for. "None" is looked for and not found,
  and blank is not looked for, as where the lengths are not consecutive.

The benches, whose names are decoded in full in [The
names](mpsc-v4-mode-waits.md#the-names):

- `min-now`: a single clock read and no ring, one thread.
- The two-thread benches are `zcr-mpsc-v4-2t-single-` and a tail, written here by the tail.
  `2t` is a sender and a receiver on two threads, and `single` a `Single` ring.
  - `so-spntfe`: a ring that can only spin, `SpinOnly`, its receiver spinning forever at an
    empty ring. "The spin-only one" in the text.
  - `sos-futex-spntfe`: a ring that can spin or sleep on a futex, `SpinOrSleep<Futex>`, its
    receiver spinning forever and so never sleeping. "The ring that can sleep" in the text.
  - `slp-futex-slptfe`: a ring that sleeps on a futex, `Sleep<Futex>`, its receiver sleeping
    until woken at every empty look.
  - `so` and `sos-futex` are those first two where a column has no room.
- Placements: `ccx` and `smt`, the CPUs given in [The sweep](#the-sweep).

## Why it was taken

Two overnight sessions on one binary, five invocations of ten runs and one of fifty, disagreed
with each other and with the session in [mpsc-v4-mode-waits.md](mpsc-v4-mode-waits.md) on
two-thread benches at cross-core placements, by more than their claims allowed. Three probes on
the 7600X `ccx` pair, on `zcr-mpsc-v4-2t-single-sos-futex-spntfe`, found what moved the time per
step. Their records are not committed:

- The environment's size does not. Padded by 0 to 4096 bytes in eleven steps, ten runs each, 107
  of 110 runs read 75.5 to 75.9 ns.
- Address randomization does not. With it off, `setarch -R`, all 40 runs read 75.5 to 75.8 ns.
- `inner` does. In the fifty-run invocation every run at 71.1 ns had sized `inner` to 6 and every
  run at 75.7 ns to 7. Fixed by hand, three alternated passes of ten runs, `--inner` 5, 6, 7 and
  8 read 73.1, 70.6, 75.5 and 67.1 ns, 27 or more of each 30 runs within 0.6 ns.

## The sweep

input.new_string:
# Random inner removes the period of 4

Two invocations of one bench could disagree by more than their claims allowed, because the
harness sizes `inner` itself and a two-thread bench's time per step depends on the value it
picks: on the 7600X `ccx` pair `zcr-mpsc-v4-2t-single-sos-futex-spntfe` reads 71.1 ns a step at
an `inner` of 6 and 75.7 ns at 7. This file holds what was taken to understand that, from `feat:
fit, the cost of a step from samples of many lengths` (2026-10-08).

- A sweep, each run at one fixed `inner` and the runs stepping it across a range, shows the
  dependence has a period of 4.
- Runs in which each sample picks its `inner` at random from a span remove the period, so the
  result no longer hangs on one value.
- They do not make every run agree: over 1-32 a run lands on one of two rates about 6 ns a step
  apart.
- `linear-regression`, `lr` for short and first named `fit`, reads both, and with the harness
  overhead of about 18 ns taken off gives a step's cost where a line holds.

Whether random `inner` makes separate invocations agree is not tested here.

-## Terms
-What is measured:
-- **Step**: the operation a bench times. For a ring one message sent and received, for `min-now`
-  one clock read.
-- **Sample**: one timed stretch, a clock read before and after `inner` steps back to back. Its
-  time, the sample time, is in ns.
-- **`inner`**: the steps in one sample, also called its length. `--inner 7` fixes it for a run,
-  `--inner 1-16` picks each sample's at random from the span, uniformly, and with neither the
-  harness sizes it. "Fixed" and "random" in the tables say which.
-- **Run**: one process measuring one bench over many samples, its result their mean.
-- **Sweep**: a set of runs that steps a fixed `inner` across a range, each run at one value. The
-  sweep here is 336 runs, two passes of three runs a bench at each value.
-- **Pass**: one time through the list of `inner` values, `a` or `b`, the second the first
-  reversed.
-- **Time per step**: a sample's time divided by `inner`, in ns, what iiac-perf reports for a
-  bench. It is a step's cost with the harness overhead shared out over the steps, `ns/op` in Go's
-  and JMH's benchmarks. The reports and the other notes call it the level until a rename reaches
-  them.
-- **Harness overhead**: what a sample costs beyond its steps, the clock reads around them, about
-  18 ns on the 7600X. It is the same whatever the bench, so it is measured once, by `min-now`.
-What `linear-regression` reports, a line fitted through sample time against `inner`:
-- **Slope**: what one more step adds to a sample, ns a step, the cost of a step where a line
-  holds.
-- **Intercept**: what a sample of no steps would take, ns. For `min-now` it is the harness
-  overhead, and for a ring the overhead plus what the ring pays once a sample.
-- **Residual**: how far a length's sample time sits from the line, ns.
-- **Halves apart**: the line refitted over the lower and the upper half of the lengths, and the
-  two slopes' difference as a percent of the whole line's slope.
-- **A line holds**: the halves are within 1% of each other, so every step costs about the same
-  whatever the length and the slope and intercept mean what they say. Otherwise no cost is
-  named.
-- **Period**: residuals that repeat with `inner` modulo some k, found in one pass and scored by
-  how much of the other pass's scatter they account for. "None" is looked for and not found,
-  and blank is not looked for, as where the lengths are not consecutive.
-The benches, whose names are decoded in full in [The
-names](mpsc-v4-mode-waits.md#the-names):
-- `min-now`: a single clock read and no ring, one thread.
-- The two-thread benches are `zcr-mpsc-v4-2t-single-` and a tail, written here by the tail.
-  `2t` is a sender and a receiver on two threads, and `single` a `Single` ring.
-  - `so-spntfe`: a ring that can only spin, `SpinOnly`, its receiver spinning forever at an
-    empty ring. "The spin-only one" in the text.
-  - `sos-futex-spntfe`: a ring that can spin or sleep on a futex, `SpinOrSleep<Futex>`, its
-    receiver spinning forever and so never sleeping. "The ring that can sleep" in the text.
-  - `slp-futex-slptfe`: a ring that sleeps on a futex, `Sleep<Futex>`, its receiver sleeping
-    until woken at every empty look.
-  - `so` and `sos-futex` are those first two where a column has no room.
-- Placements: `ccx` and `smt`, the CPUs given in [The sweep](#the-sweep).
-## Why it was taken
-The disagreement was two overnight sessions on one binary, five invocations of ten runs and one
-of fifty, against each other and against the session in
-[mpsc-v4-mode-waits.md](mpsc-v4-mode-waits.md), on two-thread benches at cross-core placements.
-Three probes on the 7600X `ccx` pair, on `sos-futex-spntfe`, found what moved the time per step.
-Their records are not committed:
-- The environment's size does not. Padded by 0 to 4096 bytes in eleven steps, ten runs each, 107
-  of 110 runs read 75.5 to 75.9 ns.
-- Address randomization does not. With it off, `setarch -R`, all 40 runs read 75.5 to 75.8 ns.
-- `inner` does. In the fifty-run invocation every run at 71.1 ns had sized `inner` to 6 and every
-  run at 75.7 ns to 7. Fixed by hand, three alternated passes of ten runs, `--inner` 5, 6, 7 and
-  8 read 73.1, 70.6, 75.5 and 67.1 ns, 27 or more of each 30 runs within 0.6 ns.
-## The sweep
-- Source: commit `a946d7c1`, jj change `rrwqouqq`, a clean tree, `feat: mpsc bench names follow
-  the ring's words`, the plain `iiac-perf` 0.28.23.
-- Binary: `7715ab993ac3b78c`, built on the 3900X.
-- Host: the 7600X, the clock pinned at 4701 MHz. `ccx` is CPUs 5 and 4, and `smt` for a
-  one-thread bench is CPU 5.
-- Two threads, on `ccx`, `--inner` 1 to 16: `zcr-mpsc-v4-2t-single-so-spntfe`,
-  `zcr-mpsc-v4-2t-single-sos-futex-spntfe`, and `zcr-mpsc-v4-2t-single-slp-futex-slptfe`.
-- One thread, on `smt`, `--inner` 20, 30, 40, 50, 60, 80, 100 and 120: `min-now`, a single clock
-  read with no ring.
-- Two passes, three runs of each bench at each `inner` in a pass, so six runs a point. A record's
-  `tags.pass` is `a` or `b`.
-- The order of `inner` in pass a is scrambled, and pass b runs it in reverse, so a drift over the
-  11.5 minutes cannot pass for an effect of `inner`.
-- Records, every switch count in them zero:
-  [records/inner-sweep-7600x.jsonl](../records/inner-sweep-7600x.jsonl), 336 runs.
-The loop, pass b taking each list reversed:
-T2="zcr-mpsc-v4-2t-single-so-spntfe zcr-mpsc-v4-2t-single-sos-futex-spntfe \
-    zcr-mpsc-v4-2t-single-slp-futex-slptfe"
-  iiac-perf $T2 --pin-cpus ccx --runs 3 --run-sleep 100-200ms --inner $i \
-    --tag pass=a --record-file inner-sweep-7600x.jsonl
-done
-  iiac-perf min-now --pin-cpus smt --runs 3 --run-sleep 100-200ms --inner $i \
-    --tag pass=a --record-file inner-sweep-7600x.jsonl
-done
-## One thread
-`min-now`, the median of six runs. A sample's time is the time per step times `inner`. The
-columns are the fixed `inner`, the time per step in ns, and the sample time in ns:
-| `inner` | ns/step | sample ns |
-The time per step falls as `inner` grows and never settles. A line through sample time against
-`inner`, fitted by hand, has a slope of 18.264 ns a step in each pass and an intercept of 18.61
-ns in pass a and 18.57 ns in pass b. So a sample costs about one clock read beyond its steps, and
-the time per step carries that cost divided by `inner`.
-## Two threads
-`zcr-mpsc-v4-2t-single-*` on `ccx`, the median of six runs. The columns are the fixed `inner`
-and each bench's time per step in ns, the bench named by its tail:
-| `inner` | `so-spntfe` | `sos-futex-spntfe` | `slp-futex-slptfe` |
-- At `inner` 1 the two spinning benches read 21 and 25 ns above their times per step at 16.
-- `sos-futex-spntfe` is low at 4, 8, 12 and 16 and high at the odd values between, a period of 4.
-  `so-spntfe` has none, only a slow wave, low at 5 and high at 9.
-- Which of the two is faster depends on `inner`: at 8 the ring that can sleep reads 3.7 ns under
-  the spin-only one, and at 7 it reads 4.7 ns over.
-- The two passes agree. The same hand fit, a simple linear regression of sample time on `inner`,
-  gives `so-spntfe` 70.48 and 70.46 ns a step and `sos-futex-spntfe` 69.61 and 69.54 ns a step.
-- A line does not describe them, though, so those slopes are not the cost of a step. The slope
-  moves with the range fitted where `min-now`'s stays at 18.26 ns over any part of its range.
-  The columns are the `inner` values the line is fitted over, then for each of the two benches
-  the slope in ns a step and the intercept in ns:
-  | `inner` fitted | `so` slope ns | intercept ns | `sos-futex` slope ns | intercept ns |
-  What changing `inner` does to a two-thread bench is a systematic effect and not noise about a
-  line, so the regression can give neither the sample's overhead nor the step's cost for them.
-- `slp-futex-slptfe` sleeps at every look, and its passes differ by up to 10% at one `inner`, so
-  this sweep says nothing of its shape.
-## Random per sample
-A run at a fixed `inner` repeats one burst length, so the sweep cannot say whether a two-thread
-bench's cost follows the length or the repetition. `--inner 1-16` picks each sample's length at
-random from the span, and the record holds the samples and their summed time at each length.
-- Source: commit `124244db`, jj change `vrxrlwwy`, a clean tree, `feat: inner drawn per sample
-  from a range`, `iiac-perf-dev` 0.28.24-2, binary `f53a7f480a66675f`, built on the 3900X.
-- The same host, placements, and benches as the sweep. Two passes of five runs, tagged `pass`,
-  - the three two-thread benches on `ccx` at `--inner 1-16` and at `--inner 1-32`
-  - `min-now` on `smt` at `--inner 20-120`
-  - the two spinning benches at `--inner 7` and at `--inner 8`, fixed, as a control on the
-    binary
-- Records, every switch count zero:
-  [records/inner-random-7600x.jsonl](../records/inner-random-7600x.jsonl), 110 runs.
-The control reads as the landed binary did: `sos-futex-spntfe` 76.0 ns at 7 and 67.0 ns at 8,
-`so-spntfe` 71.1 and 70.6 ns. So the new binary's fixed loop measures what the old one did.
-## What linear-regression says
-`iiac-perf-dev linear-regression records/inner-sweep-7600x.jsonl` and the same on
-`records/inner-random-7600x.jsonl`. The command is a simple linear regression of sample time on
-`inner`, by ordinary least squares. It refits each half of the lengths and names a cost only
-where the two slopes agree within 1%, "a line holds". The columns are the bench, its `inner`
-fixed at each value or random over the span, the slope in ns a step, the intercept in ns, the
-halves apart in percent, the period found, and whether a line holds, each as
-[Terms](#terms) says:
-| bench | `inner` | slope | intercept | halves apart % | period | a line |
-| `so-spntfe` | fixed, 1 to 16 | 70.435 | 5.78 | 5.53 | none | does not hold |
-| `so-spntfe` | random, 1-16 | 74.438 | 7.08 | 5.00 | none | does not hold |
-| `so-spntfe` | random, 1-32 | 68.165 | 25.58 | 0.95 | none | holds |
-| `sos-futex-spntfe` | fixed, 1 to 16 | 69.557 | 18.18 | 6.25 | 4 | does not hold |
-| `sos-futex-spntfe` | random, 1-16 | 76.155 | 11.96 | 2.69 | none | does not hold |
-| `sos-futex-spntfe` | random, 1-32 | 69.968 | 28.87 | 1.36 | none | does not hold |
-`slp-futex-slptfe` is left out: in all three its runs scatter too much for the halves to say.
-- One thread: both ways give `min-now` 18.26 ns a step and about 18.4 ns a sample, the two
-  slopes 0.008 ns apart. The regression holds and the two ways agree.
-- The period of 4 followed the repetition. Fixed, `sos-futex-spntfe`'s residuals by `inner`
-  modulo 4 are -31.7, +14.9, +0.3 and +16.4 ns a sample, a period that accounts for 71% of the
-  other pass's residual scatter. Random over 1-16 they are -0.9, +1.4, -0.1 and -0.4 ns, and
-  `linear-regression` finds no period in any random group.
-- What is left is smooth. A sample of one step sits 10 ns over the line for `sos-futex-spntfe`
-  and 15 ns for `so-spntfe`, the next few under it, and from about 8 steps the time per step is flat
-  to 0.3 ns. So the short lengths bend the line, and over 1-32, where they are a smaller share,
-  the halves come within 1.4%.
-- The slope depends on the span, and on the run. Over 1-16 every run of ten reads within 0.4 ns
-  of 74.4 ns a step for `so-spntfe` and of 76.2 ns for `sos-futex-spntfe`. Over 1-32 eight runs
-  of ten read 68.1 to 68.6 and 69.8 to 70.2 ns, and two read 72.3 and 74.1, and 74.6 and 74.8
-  ns. So a two-thread bench runs at one of two rates about 6 ns a step apart, a whole run at
-  one of them, and the span moves the odds. We think it is a state the two threads settle
-  into, and nothing here says what sets it.
-- At either rate the ring that can sleep reads slower than the spin-only one by about the same
-  amount, 1.7 ns a step over 1-16 and 1.8 ns over 1-32, 2.3% and 2.6%. `linear-regression`
-  names no cost for three of those four groups, so this is a pointer and not a measurement.
-So for one thread the regression gives the step's cost and the sample's overhead. For two
-threads random lengths remove the period, and what remains, a bend at short lengths and
-two rates a run may land on, still keeps a line from holding in most groups.
-## With the overhead taken off
-The harness wraps a sample in the same clock reads whatever it times, so its overhead is one
-number for a host. `linear-regression` takes it from `min-now`'s intercept, 18.53 ns from the
-fixed counts and 18.16 ns from the random lengths, and takes it off each length's sample. What
-is left over `inner` is the cost of a step at that length, the `step ns` column of the
-command's output. The columns are the bench, its `inner`, and in ns a step: the step at a length
-of 1, the lowest step and the length it falls at, and the step at the longest length:
-| bench | `inner` | step at 1 | lowest step, at | step at the longest |
-- Most of what a sample of one step read over a long one was the harness. The times per step
-  at `inner` 1 were 90.5 and 92.6 ns, 21 and 25 ns over those at 16, and with the overhead off the
-  step at 1 is 3.8 and 7.4 ns over the step at 16.
-- With random lengths, a sample of one step costs about 10 ns more than a step of a long burst,
-  for both rings. Over 1-32 `so-spntfe` holds a line, and its intercept less the overhead is
-  7.42 ns, what the ring pays once a sample. We think it is the ring starting a burst.
-- The controls at `--inner 7` and `8` are two lengths, too few to regress, and are given a step
-  by the subtraction: `so-spntfe` 68.44 and 68.14 ns, `sos-futex-spntfe` 73.36 and 64.65 ns, the
-  period of 4 still in the second.
-- Whether a clock read costs the same after a ring step as after another clock read is not
-  measured, so the overhead is `min-now`'s and is taken as the ring's.
-## What it does not hold
-- `Multi`, the `smt` pair for two threads, and `inner` past 16. A larger sweep was stopped for
-  its length, and its one pass, 800 runs, is not committed.
-- The 3900X and the Pi 5.
-- Why repeating one burst length gives the ring that can sleep a period of 4, and what sets
-  which of the two rates a run lands on.

+`records/inner-random-7600x.jsonl`. The command is a simple linear regression of sample time on
+`inner`, by ordinary least squares. It refits each half of the lengths and names a cost only
+where the two slopes agree within 1%, "a line holds". The columns are the bench, its `inner`
+fixed at each value or random over the span, the slope in ns a step, the intercept in ns, the
+halves apart in percent, the period found, and whether a line holds, each as
+[Terms](#terms) says:
+| bench | `inner` | slope | intercept | halves apart % | period | a line |
+| `so-spntfe` | fixed, 1 to 16 | 70.435 | 5.78 | 5.53 | none | does not hold |
+| `so-spntfe` | random, 1-16 | 74.438 | 7.08 | 5.00 | none | does not hold |
+| `so-spntfe` | random, 1-32 | 68.165 | 25.58 | 0.95 | none | holds |

+| `sos-futex-spntfe` | random, 1-16 | 76.155 | 11.96 | 2.69 | none | does not hold |

+- The period of 4 followed the repetition. Fixed, `sos-futex-spntfe`'s residuals by `inner`

+  and 15 ns for `so-spntfe`, the next few under it, and from about 8 steps the time per step is flat
+  to 0.3 ns. So the short lengths bend the line, and over 1-32, where they are a smaller share,

+## With the overhead taken off

+number for a host. `linear-regression` takes it from `min-now`'s intercept, 18.53 ns from the
+fixed counts and 18.16 ns from the random lengths, and takes it off each length's sample. What
+is left over `inner` is the cost of a step at that length, the `step ns` column of the
+command's output. The columns are the bench, its `inner`, and in ns a step: the step at a length
+of 1, the lowest step and the length it falls at, and the step at the longest length:
+| bench | `inner` | step at 1 | lowest step, at | step at the longest |

+  by the subtraction: `so-spntfe` 68.44 and 68.14 ns, `sos-futex-spntfe` 73.36 and 64.65 ns, the
+  period of 4 still in the second.
+- Whether a clock read costs the same after a ring step as after another clock read is not
+  measured, so the overhead is `min-now`'s and is taken as the ring's.

+- The 3900X and the Pi 5.
+- Why repeating one burst length gives the ring that can sleep a period of 4, and what sets

input.old_str:
# An inner sweep on the 7600X

A bench's time per step is a sample's time divided by `inner`, the steps timed back to back in
the sample, and the harness sizes `inner` by itself in every run. This file holds a sweep that
fixes `inner` by hand over a range, to show what the time per step does as it changes, from
`feat: fit, the cost of a step from samples of many lengths` (2026-10-08). The records are what
the `linear-regression` subcommand, `lr` for short and first named `fit`, is written against.
Below the sweep are runs that pick each sample's `inner` at random, taken once the harness could,
and what `linear-regression` says of both.
input.new_str:
# Random inner removes the period of 4

Two invocations of one bench could disagree by more than their claims allowed, because the
harness sizes `inner` itself and a two-thread bench's time per step depends on the value it
picks: on the 7600X `ccx` pair `zcr-mpsc-v4-2t-single-sos-futex-spntfe` reads 71.1 ns a step at
an `inner` of 6 and 75.7 ns at 7. This file holds what was taken to understand that, from `feat:
fit, the cost of a step from samples of many lengths` (2026-10-08).

- A sweep, each run at one fixed `inner` and the runs stepping it across a range, shows the
  dependence has a period of 4.
- Runs in which each sample picks its `inner` at random from a span remove the period, so the
  result no longer hangs on one value.
- They do not make every run agree: over 1-32 a run lands on one of two rates about 6 ns a step
  apart.
- `linear-regression`, `lr` for short and first named `fit`, reads both, and with the harness
  overhead of about 18 ns taken off gives a step's cost where a line holds.

Whether random `inner` makes separate invocations agree is not tested here.

### The period of 4 in a can-sleep ring's level

A two-thread bench on a ring that can sleep reads low when `inner`, the steps timed back to back
in one sample, is a multiple of 4, and high when it is odd (wink, 2026-10-08, after the overnight
sessions on the landed names disagreed with the first session). The harness sizes `inner` by
itself in every run, so the level a bench reports depends on where that sizing lands.

The sweep, 7600X, `zcr-mpsc-v4-2t-single-*-spntfe`, `--inner` fixed, five runs each, level in ns.
The records are in `tmp/layout-7600x/` on the 3900X, not committed:

| `inner` | `so`, ccx | `sos-futex`, ccx | `sos-futex`, smt |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 90.6 | 93.0 | 62.6 |
| 2 | 75.2 | 78.0 | 53.6 |
| 3 | 69.0 | 74.8 | 50.9 |
| 4 | 68.9 | 70.5 | 48.3 |
| 5 | 67.7 | 73.0 | 48.8 |
| 6 | 69.3 | 70.5 | 47.7 |
| 7 | 71.1 | 75.5 | 48.9 |
| 8 | 70.2 | 67.1 | 46.4 |
| 9 | 73.1 | 75.1 | 48.9 |
| 10 | 72.9 | 71.8 | 47.7 |
| 11 | 72.5 | 74.0 | 48.3 |
| 12 | 71.8 | 68.9 | 45.9 |
| 13 | 71.3 | 72.6 | 47.8 |
| 14 | 70.7 | 71.2 | 47.3 |
| 15 | 70.1 | 71.4 | 47.2 |
| 16 | 69.2 | 68.1 | 45.9 |

What is established:

- the level follows `inner` and nothing else tried. Thirty runs each at 5, 6, 7 and 8 on the ccx
  pair read 73.1, 70.6, 75.5 and 67.1 ns, 27 or more of each 30 within 0.6 ns
- the environment's size does not move it, padded from 0 to 4096 bytes, and neither does turning
  address randomization off
- the spin-only ring shows no period of 4, only a slow wave, low at 5 and high at 9
- `min-now` shows no period at all, only the framing slope that [fit][85] is opened for,
  so the period is not the harness alone
- the same two levels came up for `zcr-mpsc-v3-2t-single-futex-spntfe` in the sessions, 71.6 ns at
  `inner` 6 and 76.1 ns at 7, so v3's `Futex` shows it as v4's `SpinOrSleep<Futex>` does

Since, from `feat: fit, the cost of a step from samples of many lengths`
([random-inner.md](notes/random-inner.md)):

- the period follows the repetition of one length and not the length. With `inner` random per
  sample from 1-16 the residuals by `inner` modulo 4 are within 1.4 ns a sample, where fixed
  they run from -31.7 to +16.4, and `fit` finds no period in any random group
- a second thing came out: over 1-32 a run lands on one of two rates about 6 ns a step apart,
  eight runs of ten on the lower, and over 1-16 all ten on the upper. Nothing says what sets it

What is not:

- what sets which of the two rates a run lands on, and whether it is what [Name what sets a
  process's level](#name-what-sets-a-processs-level) saw
- whether `Multi` shows it. On the 3900X ccx pair `zcr-mpsc-v4-2t-multi-2seg-sos-futex-spntfe`
  read 127.2 ns at `inner` 5 and 123.7 ns at 6, which says `inner` moves it, not that the period
  is 4
- whether the period belongs to the ring or to the bench's step around it
- the cause. We think it is a message's position in a 64-byte cache line, each sample starting at
  the same position when `inner` is a multiple of 4

The work:

- read the ring's layout and the bench step for what repeats every 4 messages, which needs no
  machine time
- the same sweep over `Multi`, over `slp-futex`, and on the 3900X and the Pi 5
- say whether [Name what sets a process's level](#name-what-sets-a-processs-level) is this: its
  60.6 and 76.0 ns levels on the 7600X were never checked against `inner`
- then decide how a session holds `inner`: fixed per bench, or random per sample from a range of 8
  or more consecutive values so the period averages out, the range written into the record
- until then no difference under 12% between two two-thread benches on a cross-core pair is
  carried, and the tables in [mpsc-v4-mode-waits.md](notes/mpsc-v4-mode-waits.md) are not rebuilt

content.text:
The numbers don't match because the table and the bullet come from different sets of runs, and the entry doesn't say so. The period is there, but a downward trend hides it in a table.

**Where each number comes from.** On the 7600X `ccx` pair there are three separate collections:

| collection | runs at each `inner` | sos-futex at 5, 6, 7, 8 |
|---|---|---|
| the entry's table: the large sweep, stopped partway, in `tmp/layout-7600x/` and not committed | 5 | 73.0, 70.5, 75.5, 67.1 |
| the bullet: an earlier probe at 5 to 8 only, three alternated passes of ten | 30 | 73.1, 70.6, 75.5, 67.1 |
| the committed sweep, `records/inner-fixed-7600x.jsonl` | 6 | 73.0, 70.6, 75.7, 66.9 |

So the bullet isn't summarizing the table. It's a separate check that agrees with it to within 0.1 ns, and the agreement across three collections is actually the strongest evidence that the effect is real. The entry should say this: give the table's source and the bullet's source separately.

**Why the period is hard to see.** In the `sos-futex, ccx` column, each `inner` value falls into one of four groups by its remainder when divided by 4:
- multiples of 4 (4, 8, 12, 16): 70.5, 67.1, 68.9, 68.1, the low ones
- odd values (5, 7, 9, 11, 13, 15): 73.0, 75.5, 75.1, 74.0, 72.6, 71.4, the high ones
- 2 more than a multiple of 4 (6, 10, 14): 70.5, 71.8, 71.2, in between

On top of that, every value drifts down as `inner` grows. That's the harness overhead being shared over more steps, a curve of about 18 ns divided by `inner`. The drift is as large as the pattern, so reading down the column you see a falling curve with a wobble on it. Take the trend off and the pattern is plain: the committed sweep's residuals by remainder are -31.7, +14.9, +0.3 and +16.4 ns a sample.

**A graph would settle it.** What I'd draw, for each two-thread bench on `ccx`:
1. **Time per step against `inner`, every run as a dot**, not medians, coloured by the remainder mod 4, fixed runs and random runs side by side. This shows the spread, the trend, and the colour bands of the period together.
2. **The same with the trend removed:** each length's distance from the fitted line, or the step time with the 18 ns overhead taken off. Here the period should stand out as four coloured levels for fixed `inner` and collapse to one band for random `inner`.
3. **One dot per random run of its slope, over 1-16 and 1-32.** This shows the two rates about 6 ns apart.

The committed records hold everything for this: 336 fixed runs and 110 random runs, which keep a total for each length. The entry's table comes from the uncommitted partial sweep, so a graph of all the data would either use the committed sweep or first commit those records.

**How to make it** is your call. Options:
- add panels to `iiac-perf figures`, so the graph can be redrawn from the records
- a one-off script in `tmp/`, quickest, nothing committed
- an interactive page you can hover over

A committed graph belongs in `notes/random-inner.md`, and that's more than this docs step is about, so it would be a step inserted after this one, or a Todo entry. The fix to the period-of-4 entry is a small, separate change: label where each number comes from.

In short: the table and the bullet are two separate measurements that agree; the period is real but hidden under a downward trend; a graph with the trend removed would show it at once.

content.text:
Adding the graphs to `iiac-perf figures` is very doable, and it's what the project is already heading towards. I'd do it as its own cycle after this one closes, as you suggest.

**Why it fits:**
- **The direction is already set.** `src/figures.rs` opens with "pictures of what records hold, drawn by the tool, so no script keeps a second copy of the arithmetic". A Todo entry is already moving the seven Python figures of `docs/statistics.md` into the tool so that `make.py` can be deleted. A new Python script would work against that.
- **The drawing machinery exists** (646 lines): hand-written SVG with panels, axes, ticks and a palette, PNG output through `resvg` with a bundled font, and no plotting dependency.
- **The arithmetic exists.** `src/linear_regression.rs` already reads both kinds of record (fixed counts, and random spans with their per-length totals), fits the line, takes the overhead off, and computes the residuals and the period. A figure would call that code rather than redo it, so what the graph shows and what `lr` prints can't disagree.

**What's missing:**
- `figures` draws one kind of picture: a line for each run of its block means over time. These graphs need dots as well as lines, colour by a category (`inner` mod 4), a small legend, and a way to choose which figure to draw. Either a `--figure block-means|inner|residuals|slopes` option, or a separate command word. That's a refactor of `svg()` and `Panel`.
- Three new figures:
  1. time per step against `inner`, every run as a dot, coloured by mod 4, fixed and random side by side
  2. the same with the trend removed, as residuals or as step time with the overhead off
  3. one dot per random run of its slope, to show the two rates

Roughly 400 to 600 lines with tests. As a cycle that's three or four steps: the panel refactor, the figures one or two at a time, then committing the SVGs to `notes/random-inner.md` with their text.

**If you want to see the data sooner:** I could draw graph 1 and graph 2 once as a throwaway, from the committed records, before the cycle starts, and you'd decide which views are worth building. It would either be a quick script in `tmp/` or an interactive page you can hover over. Nothing would be committed, and it would be thrown away when the Rust figures land. It's optional, since the cycle stands without it.

**For this cycle:** the fix you spotted in the period-of-4 entry, saying where the table's numbers and the bullet's numbers come from, is a few lines of `TODO.md`. It fits this docs step. The graphs would go into `## Todo` as an entry for the next cycle.

Shall I add the source labels and the graphs Todo entry in this step? And do you want the throwaway graph first?

"""Throwaway: time per step against inner, every run, on the 7600X ccx pair.

usage: python3 -I inner_graph.py <repo root> <out dir>
"""
import glob
import json
import os
import sys

import matplotlib

matplotlib.use("Agg")
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

ROOT, OUT = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2]
TMP = os.path.join(ROOT, "tmp/layout-7600x")
OVERHEAD_FIXED, OVERHEAD_RANDOM = 18.53, 18.16
BENCHES = ["zcr-mpsc-v4-2t-single-so-spntfe", "zcr-mpsc-v4-2t-single-sos-futex-spntfe"]
MOD4 = ["#d62728", "#1f77b4", "#2ca02c", "#ff7f0e"]  # inner % 4 == 0, 1, 2, 3


def read(paths):
    for p in paths:
        with open(p) as f:
            for line in f:
                if line.strip():
                    yield json.loads(line)


def fixed(paths, label):
    out = []
    for r in read(paths):
        if r.get("inner_lo") not in (None, r["inner"]) or r.get("inner_hi") not in (None, r["inner"]):
            continue
        if r.get("pin_placement") != "ccx" or r["bench"] not in BENCHES:
            continue
        out.append((label, r["bench"], r["inner"], r["mean_ns"]))
    return out


collections = [
    ("committed sweep, 6 a value", [os.path.join(ROOT, "records/inner-fixed-7600x.jsonl")]),
    ("period-of-4 table probe, 5 a value", sorted(glob.glob(os.path.join(TMP, "swp-*-ccx-*.jsonl")))),
    ("inner probe 5-8, 30 a value", sorted(glob.glob(os.path.join(TMP, "inn-*.jsonl")))),
    ("stopped large sweep", [os.path.join(TMP, "partial-big-sweep-7600x.jsonl")]),
]
MARK = ["o", "s", "D", "^"]
pts = []
for label, paths in collections:
    pts += fixed(paths, label)

rand = []
for r in read([os.path.join(ROOT, "records/inner-random-7600x.jsonl")]):
    if r.get("pin_placement") != "ccx" or r["bench"] not in BENCHES:
        continue
    lo, hi = r.get("inner_lo"), r.get("inner_hi")
    if lo is None or lo == hi:
        continue
    per = []
    for i, (n, s) in enumerate(zip(r["inner_samples"], r["inner_sum_ns"])):
        if n:
            per.append((lo + i, s / n))
    rand.append((r["bench"], f"{lo}-{hi}", per))

for name, off in (("raw", False), ("overhead-off", True)):
    fig, axes = plt.subplots(2, 2, figsize=(15, 10), sharey="row")
    for col, bench in enumerate(BENCHES):
        tail = bench.replace("zcr-mpsc-v4-2t-single-", "")
        ax = axes[0][col]
        for k, (label, _) in enumerate(collections):
            sel = [(i, m) for (l, b, i, m) in pts if l == label and b == bench]
            if not sel:
                continue
            xs = [i + (k - 1.5) * 0.12 for i, _ in sel]
            ys = [((m * i - OVERHEAD_FIXED) / i) if off else m for i, m in sel]
            cs = [MOD4[i % 4] for i, _ in sel]
            ax.scatter(xs, ys, c=cs, marker=MARK[k], s=18, alpha=0.75, label=label)
        ax.set_title(f"{tail}, fixed inner, colour = inner mod 4 (red 0, blue 1, green 2, orange 3)")
        ax.set_xlabel("inner")
        ax.set_ylabel("ns/step" + (" less 18.53 ns overhead" if off else ""))
        ax.set_xlim(0, 33)
        ax.grid(alpha=0.3)
        leg = ax.legend(fontsize=8, loc="upper right")
        for h in leg.legend_handles:
            h.set_color("#555")
        ax = axes[1][col]
        for b, span, per in rand:
            if b != bench:
                continue
            xs = [i for i, _ in per]
            ys = [((s - OVERHEAD_RANDOM) / i) if off else s / i for i, s in per]
            colour = "#1f77b4" if span == "1-16" else "#9467bd"
            ax.plot(xs, ys, color=colour, alpha=0.5, lw=1)
            ax.scatter(xs, ys, c=[MOD4[i % 4] for i in xs], s=8, zorder=3)
        ax.plot([], [], color="#1f77b4", label="random 1-16, a line a run")
        ax.plot([], [], color="#9467bd", label="random 1-32, a line a run")
        ax.set_title(f"{tail}, random inner per sample, dots coloured by inner mod 4")
        ax.set_xlabel("inner")
        ax.set_ylabel("ns/step" + (" less 18.16 ns overhead" if off else ""))
        ax.set_xlim(0, 33)
        ax.grid(alpha=0.3)
        ax.legend(fontsize=8, loc="upper right")
    for row in axes:
        lo = min(a.get_ylim()[0] for a in row)
        hi = min(max(a.get_ylim()[1] for a in row), 100 if not off else 90)
        for a in row:
            a.set_ylim(lo, hi)
    fig.suptitle(f"7600X ccx pair, time per step against inner, every run ({name})")
    fig.tight_layout()
    path = os.path.join(OUT, f"inner-{name}.png")
    fig.savefig(path, dpi=110)
    print(path)

from collections import Counter
print(Counter((l, b.replace("zcr-mpsc-v4-2t-single-", "")) for l, b, _, _ in pts))
print(Counter((b.replace("zcr-mpsc-v4-2t-single-", ""), s) for b, s, _ in rand))

content.text:
The throwaway graphs are drawn. While doing them I found that something I told you earlier was wrong.

**Correction:** the period-of-4 entry's table does not come from the stopped large sweep. It comes from a separate probe, `tmp/layout-7600x/swp-*-NN.jsonl`, five runs at each value. So there are four fixed collections on the `ccx` pair, not three. The graph plots all four, and they agree.

**The graphs:**
- `/home/wink/data/prgs/rust/iiac-perf/tmp/inner-raw.png`: time per step against `inner`
- `/home/wink/data/prgs/rust/iiac-perf/tmp/inner-overhead-off.png`: the same with the 18 ns harness overhead taken off

In each, the top row is fixed `inner`: every run is a dot, the marker shape says which collection it came from, and the colour is `inner` mod 4. The bottom row is random `inner`: one line per run, a dot at each length.

**What they show:**
- **The period of 4 is plain.** For `sos-futex-spntfe` with fixed `inner`, the red dots (multiples of 4: 4, 8, 12, 16) are the low points of a zigzag, with the odd values above them. With the overhead off it reads as a sawtooth. `so-spntfe` has no zigzag, just a slow wave.
- **The collections agree.** The committed sweep, the period-of-4 probe and the 30-run probe at 5 to 8 sit on top of each other to well under 1 ns. The stopped large sweep agrees too, apart from a dozen or so outliers, high and scattered, that only it has. We think something on the host disturbed it, which may be another reason it was stopped.
- **Random `inner` removes the zigzag.** The lines are smooth, and the colours alternate along them without moving them.
- **The two rates are obvious.** Over 1-32, most runs follow a lower curve at about 69 to 70 ns and two follow an upper one at about 75 ns. Every 1-16 run is on the upper one. The upper curve isn't flat: with the overhead off it climbs from about 73 ns at length 4 to 76 ns at 16, which is why a line doesn't hold over 1-16.

**Committing the data.** Line 217 refers to the probes' records. Everything uncommitted is in `tmp/layout-7600x/`, about 7.7 MB without the duplicate sweep copy. The `records/` directory already holds about 90 MB.

| files | what | runs |
|---|---|---|
| `swp-{so,sos-futex}-ccx-NN`, `swp-sos-futex-smt-NN` | the period-of-4 entry's table | 240 |
| `inn-{5..8}-{a,b,c}` | the 30-run probe at 5 to 8 | 120 |
| `lay-NNNN-{a,r,s}` | environment padding 0 to 4096, and address randomization off | 140 |
| `mn-NN-{a,b}`, `mn-auto` | `min-now` at fixed 10 to 42, the cycle's opening 18.27 + 18.47/`inner` | 183 |
| `partial-big-sweep-7600x` | the stopped large sweep | 800 |

`inner-sweep-7600x.jsonl` in that directory is byte-identical to the committed `records/inner-fixed-7600x.jsonl`, so it would be left out. I'd copy the rest into `records/probes-7600x-20261008/` with the file names unchanged, plus a short `README.md` saying what each group is and which text cites it. This step would then update line 217 and the period-of-4 entry to link to them.

**One question first:** in `lay-NNNN-{a,r,s}`, what do the `a`, `r` and `s` suffixes mean? The records carry no tags, and I can't tell from them. `r` is probably address randomization off (`setarch -R`), but I don't know what `s` is.

The overnight sessions of 2026-10-08 in `tmp/session-*-20261008/`, from the continuation notes, are also uncommitted, but they belong to the v4 note's held tables. I'd leave them out of this step unless you want them in.

In short: the graph shows the period of 4 clearly, shows that all four fixed collections agree, and shows random `inner` smoothing it out and splitting into two rates. To commit the probe data I just need the meaning of `a`, `r` and `s`.

TEXT: Close, but it is a moon we can find. The effect is deterministic. It just depends on something we don't record: the addresses the program's data lands at.

**Why addresses can matter**

- The kernel copies the arguments and environment onto the top of the stack before the program starts. A longer command line pushes every stack address down by that many bytes.
- A rebuilt binary with different string lengths moves static data and sometimes code.
- Address randomization then adds a random offset per process.

Any of these can change whether two hot variables share a cache line, whether a load and a store 4,096 bytes apart collide in the CPU's address check, or which branch-predictor entries two branches share. Each of those costs a fixed few percent, either there or not, which is the two-level pattern we see.

This is a known trap. Mytkowicz and others showed in 2009 that changing the size of the environment alone moved benchmark results by several percent, enough to reverse a conclusion.

**How it fits our data**

- 7600X: the level changes per run with the same binary and command, which fits the per-process random offset. The command line changed the odds, from 2 in 100 low to about 35 in 50 low.
- 3900X: the level is steady for one binary and command and moves when either changes.
- Only pairs sharing a cache show it. The smt pairs and the Pi 5 do not.

**What is not established**

That this is the cause here. It fits, and I have not tested it. The 3900X case is odd under t

    if n == "inner-sweep-7600x.jsonl": continue

    print(g, len(rs), dict(vs), ts[0], ts[-1], dict(cpus)); print("   ", dict(benches))
E

# Probes on the 7600X, 2026-10-08

The records of the probes that found `inner` moves a two-thread bench's time per step, taken
before the sweep in [random-inner.md](../../notes/random-inner.md) and cited by it and by
`TODO.md`. Each file is one invocation, its name the setting it ran at.

- Source: commit `a946d7c1`, jj change `rrwqouqq`, the plain `iiac-perf` 0.28.23, binary
  `7715ab993ac3b78c`, built on the 3900X.
- Host: the 7600X, the clock pinned at 4701 MHz. `ccx` is CPUs 5 and 4, `smt` CPUs 5 and 11.
- Every run `--run-sleep 100-200ms`, ten runs an invocation unless said. `$B` is
  `zcr-mpsc-v4-2t-single-sos-futex-spntfe`.
- The files were written on the 7600X under `~/iiac-perf-data/` and each record carries that
  path. They were copied here unchanged.

## The environment's size and address randomization, `lay-*`

`lay-NNNN-a.jsonl`, 110 runs, 14:44Z to 14:49Z: `$B` on `ccx`, the environment padded by a
variable `PAD` of `NNNN` bytes, 0 to 4096 in eleven steps, address randomization on, the
default. The `inner` is the harness's own.

`lay-NNNN-r.jsonl` and `lay-NNNN-s.jsonl`, 40 runs: the same at 0 and 64 bytes with address
randomization off, `setarch -R`, `r` and `s` being two invocations of it.

```
for n in 0000 0008 0016 0032 0064 0128 0256 0512 1024 2048 4096; do
  PAD=$(head -c $((10#$n)) /dev/zero | tr "\0" x) iiac-perf $B --pin-cpus ccx \
    --run-sleep 100-200ms --record-file lay-$n-a.jsonl
done
for n in 0000 0064; do for r in r s; do
  PAD=$(head -c $((10#$n)) /dev/zero | tr "\0" x) setarch -R iiac-perf $B --pin-cpus ccx \
    --run-sleep 100-200ms --record-file lay-$n-$r.jsonl
done; done
```

## `inner` fixed at 5 to 8, `inn-*`

`inn-I-P.jsonl`, 120 runs, 14:50Z to 14:54Z: `$B` on `ccx` at `--inner I`, three passes `P`
of `a`, `b`, `c`, each pass in the order 6, 7, 5, 8. Thirty runs a value.

```
for p in a b c; do for i in 6 7 5 8; do
  iiac-perf $B --pin-cpus ccx --run-sleep 100-200ms --inner $i --record-file inn-$i-$p.jsonl
done; done
```

## `inner` fixed at 1 to 16, `swp-*`

`swp-W-PL-II.jsonl`, 240 runs, 15:01Z to 15:09Z, the table in `TODO.md`'s entry "The period of 4
in a can-sleep ring's level": five runs at each `--inner` from 1 to 16, ascending, of three
cases, `so` on `ccx`, `sos-futex` on `ccx`, and `sos-futex` on `smt`.

```
for i in 01 02 03 04 05 06 07 08 09 10 11 12 13 14 15 16; do
  for c in so:ccx sos-futex:ccx sos-futex:smt; do w=${c%%:*}; pl=${c##*:}
    iiac-perf zcr-mpsc-v4-2t-single-$w-spntfe --pin-cpus $pl --runs 5 \
      --run-sleep 100-200ms --inner $((10#$i)) --record-file swp-$w-$pl-$i.jsonl
  done
done
```

## `min-now` at fixed `inner`, `mn-*`

`mn-auto.jsonl`, three runs at the harness's own `inner`, 21. `mn-I-P.jsonl`, 180 runs, 15:09Z
to 15:16Z: `min-now` on `smt` at `--inner` 10, 14, 18, 20, 21, 22, 24, 30, and 42, two passes,
the source of the cycle's `18.27 + 18.47 / inner` ns.

```
for p in a b; do for i in 10 14 18 20 21 22 24 30 42; do
  iiac-perf min-now --pin-cpus smt --run-sleep 100-200ms --inner $i --record-file mn-$i-$p.jsonl
done; done
```

## The stopped large sweep, `partial-big-sweep-7600x.jsonl`

800 runs, 16:08Z to 16:35Z: pass `a` of a sweep of five two-thread benches on `smt` and `ccx`,
five runs at each of 24 `inner` values from 1 to 24 in a scrambled order, stopped after 16 of
them for its length. `Single` and `Multi` over one segment, each over `SpinOnly` and
`SpinOrSleep<Futex>` spinning forever, and `Single` over `Sleep<Futex>`:

```
T2="zcr-mpsc-v4-2t-single-so-spntfe zcr-mpsc-v4-2t-single-sos-futex-spntfe \
    zcr-mpsc-v4-2t-multi-1seg-so-spntfe zcr-mpsc-v4-2t-multi-1seg-sos-futex-spntfe \
    zcr-mpsc-v4-2t-single-slp-futex-slptfe"
for i in 13 4 22 9 1 18 7 24 11 2 16 5 20 14 3 23 8 12 19 6 21 10 17 15; do
  iiac-perf $T2 --pin-cpus smt,ccx --runs 5 --run-sleep 100-200ms --inner $i --tag pass=a \
    --record-file inner-sweep-7600x.jsonl
done
```

It was renamed `partial-big-sweep-7600x.jsonl` when stopped. On the `ccx` pair a dozen or so of
its runs read well above the other collections at the same `inner`, which none of them show.
